If there was an increase of 24% in the average number of vehicles (in thousands) manufactured by company B during 2011 to 2014) with respect to number of vehicles manufacured by company A in 2009. then how many vehicles (in thousands) did company A manufacture in 2009?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Total number of vehicles manufactured by company B during 2011 to 2014 = 270 + 250 + 289 + 310 = 1119 thousand

The average number of vehicles manufactured by company B during 2011 to 2014 = 1119/4 = 279.75 thousand

Number of vehicles manufactured by company A in 2009 = 279.75 × 100/(100 + 24) = 225.60 thousand

**∴ number of vehicles manufactured by company A in 2009 is 225.60 thousand**

questions.question:
The line chart given below shows the expenditure of two companies R and S in different years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e01f58ef9bd963206ca0bf95beae1fdcecd9234a6b2766d16f2ad1c73bbb359e.png] 

Which of the following statement is NOT correct?

I. The expenditure of R in year Y1 and Y2 together is (Approximate) 81.66 percent of the expenditure of S in year Y3 and Y4 together

II. The total expenditure of company S is (Approximate) 112.12 percent of the total expenditure of company R.
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Statement I:

The expenditure of R in year Y1 and Y2 together = 600 + 500 = 1100

The expenditure of S in year Y3 and Y4 together = 700 + 500 = 1200

Percentage of the expenditure of R in year Y1 and Y2 together to the expenditure of S in year Y3 and Y4 together = 1100/1200 × 100 = 91.66%

Statement I is not correct.

Statement II:

Total expenditure of company S = 1200 + 900 + 700 + 500 + 400 = 3700

Total expenditure of company R = 600 + 500 + 800 + 400 + 1000 = 3300

Percentage of the total expenditure of company S to the total expenditure of company R = 3700/3300 × 100 = 112.12%

Statement II is correct.

**∴ Option 2 is the correct answer.**

questions.question:

If the exports of Company M in 2008 were Rs. 210 crores, what were the imports of the company in the same year?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Exports of Company M in 2008 = Rs. 210 crores

Ratio of imports to exports for Company M in 2008 = 1.4 (from the graph)

**Formula used:**

Imports = Exports × Ratio of imports to exports

**Calculation:**

Imports = 210 × 1.4

⇒ Imports = 294 crores

**∴ The imports of Company M in 2008 were Rs. 294 crores.**

questions.question:
Read the given information and answer the question that follows.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f38a8c67132ac7152b63c9872a937eab63ac710c1c51ba64bf8ffe20097f2ce5.png] 

If Company A makes 25% of income as profit in 2014, then its expenditure in that year is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Income of Company A (2014) = ₹40 crores

Profit percentage = 25%

**Formula used:**

Profit% = (R - E)/E × 100

Where R = Revenue, E = Expenditure

**Calculation:**

Profit% = (R - E)/E × 100

⇒ 25 = (40 - E) / E × 100

⇒ E = (40 - E) × 4

⇒ E = 160 - 4E

⇒ 5E = 160

⇒ E = 160 / 5 = 32 crores

**∴ The expenditure of Company A in 2014 is ₹32 crores.**

questions.question:
The line chart given below shows production of sugar by two companies A and B in 5 years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b165f223542252e7aa539a8d6d7fae77f8d91d7f3af8ac04782655744793e689.png] 

Which of the following statement is correct?

I. The production of sugar by A in years J and K together is 7.69 percent more the production of sugar by B in year L and M together.

II. The ratio of combined production of sugar by B in years M and N to the combined production of sugar by A in years K and L is 21 ∶ 16.
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

I. The production of sugar by A in years J and K together is 7.69 percent **more** the production of sugar by B in year L and M together.

Production of sugar by A in years J and K together = 70 + 50 = 120

Production of sugar by B in year L and M together = 70 + 60 = 130

According to the question:

130 - 120 = 10

10/130 = 7.69%

The production of sugar by A in years J and K together is 7.69% **less** than the production of sugar by B in years L and M together.

Statement I is wrong.

II. The ratio of combined production of sugar by B in years M and N to the combined production of sugar by A in years K and L is 21 ∶ 16.

Production of sugar by B in years M and N = 60 + 45 = 105

Production of sugar by A in years K and L = 50 + 30 = 80

Ratio = 105 : 80 = 21 : 16

Statement II is correct.

**∴ Option 1 is the correct answer.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6aacb9a90ba523740d5fe4d2e9457c37dcb2fc100319e352a4a3772da980d3b5.png] 

Which of the following statement is correct?

I. The combined cost price of J and K is 100 percent more than the combined profit of L and M.

II. The ratio of combined profit of N and P to the combined cost price of K and M is 2 ∶ 1.
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Statement I:

The combined cost price of J and K = 650 + 550 = 1200

The combined profit of L and M = 250 + 350 = 600

The combined cost price of J and K is more than the combined profit of L and M by (1200 - 600) = 600, which is 100 percent of the combined profit of L and M.

Statement I is true.

Statement II:

Combined profit of N and P = 200 + 300 = 500

Combined cost price of K and M = 550 + 450 = 1000

Ratio = 500 : 1000 = 1 : 2

Statement II is wrong.

**∴ Option 2 is the correct answer.**

Average expenditure of company J in year A and B = (400 + 300)/2 = 350

Average expenditure of company K in year C and D = (500 + 300)/2 = 400

L1 = The difference between average expenditure of company J in year A and B and the average expenditure of company K in year C and D

L1 = 400 - 350 = 50

L2 = The value of average expenditure of company K in all 5 years,

L2 = (1000 + 700 + 500 + 300 + 200)/5 = 2700/5 = 540

The value of (L2 - L1) = 540 - 50 = 490

**∴ Option 1 is the correct answer.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b90bf548ab0d3f07dd5b3d1cefcabf0671698e0180501e4167753b9cbca2ae51.png] 

What is the depreciation of the car from 2001 to 2007 in percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Initial value of the car in 2001 = $24,000

Final value of the car in 2007 = $5,800

**Formula used:**

Depreciation percentage = ((Initial value - Final value) / Initial value) × 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ Depreciation percentage = ((24,000 - 5,800) / 24,000) × 100

⇒ Depreciation percentage = (18,200 / 24,000) × 100

⇒ Depreciation percentage = 75.83%

**∴ The depreciation of the car from 2001 to 2007 is 75.83%.**
